title: Code review
context_summary: Section 'Overview' of the 'Code review' handbook page.
text:
Every change ships through a pull request. There are no direct pushes
to the `main` branch — the branch protection rule rejects them and the
`protect-main` pre-push hook catches the mistake before it reaches the
remote.

title: Code review
context_summary: Draft PRs early. Conventional Commits title format under 70 characters.
text:
Open a pull request as soon as the change compiles and the tests pass.
Draft pull requests are encouraged: opening early gives CI a chance to
catch problems while the change is still cheap to redirect.

The pull request title follows Conventional Commits: a type prefix
(`feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`), an optional scope
in parentheses, and an imperative subject under 70 characters.

title: Code review
context_summary: One reviewer for in-package changes, two for cross-package or deploy-pipeline changes. Focus on interface, not style.
text:
Every pull request needs one review from a maintainer of the touched
package. Two reviews are required for changes that cross package
boundaries or modify the deployment pipeline.

Reviewers focus on the change's interface, not its style — the
formatter and linter handle style. If style still drifts, open a
follow-up pull request against the linter configuration rather than
litigating it in the review.

title: Code review
context_summary: Squash-merge by default; rebase-merge only for hot-fix branches to preserve timestamps.
text:
Pull requests use squash-merge. The squash commit takes its message
from the pull request title and body so the linear history stays
greppable.

Hot-fix branches are the only exception: they use rebase-merge so the
original commit timestamp is preserved for the post-incident report.

title: Deployment
context_summary: Section 'Overview' of the 'Deployment' handbook page.
text:
Tlaltipac ships every weekday. The release pipeline is fully
automated; the only manual step is the release notes write-up that
the release captain posts to the customer changelog.

title: Deployment
context_summary: Every merge to main goes to staging; production after 30 minutes green. Image SHA pinned end-to-end.
text:
Every merge to `main` triggers a build, a full test run, and a
deployment to the staging environment. The deploy job pins the image
SHA, so the build the team validates in staging is byte-identical to
the one that reaches production.

A deploy to production runs once the staging environment has been
green for thirty minutes. Engineers can promote earlier through the
release tooling if the change is urgent.

title: Deployment
context_summary: Rollback is one make command and auto-opens an incident ticket. Flag every rollback in #engineering.
text:
A rollback is one command: `make rollback service=<name>` reverts the
named service to its previous image. The command also opens an
incident ticket automatically so the rollback is tracked alongside the
underlying bug.

Never rollback without flagging it in `#engineering`. Even if the
change looks isolated, another engineer may be waiting for the new
build to test their own change.

title: Deployment
context_summary: Release captain rotates weekly; owns deploy review, customer release notes, and incident point-of-contact.
text:
The release captain rotates weekly. The captain owns the morning
deploy review, writes the customer-facing release notes, and is the
primary point of contact for any incident that happens during their
shift.

The schedule lives in the team calendar; the engineer on rotation
receives a calendar invite for the week.

title: Developer environment
context_summary: Section 'Overview' of the 'Developer environment' handbook page.
text:
The Tlaltipac monorepo targets Python 3.14 and Node 22. Every service
boots locally on a laptop without external infrastructure other than a
Postgres container.

title: Developer environment
context_summary: Local-toolchain bootstrap: install uv and pnpm, run make bootstrap once, idempotent thereafter.
text:
Install `uv` for Python dependency management and `pnpm` for the
TypeScript packages. Clone the monorepo and run `make bootstrap`; the
target installs every language toolchain, runs database migrations
against a local Postgres container, and seeds fixtures.

The bootstrap target is idempotent. Re-run it whenever a dependency
manifest changes.

title: Developer environment
context_summary: Local stack via docker compose: Postgres, Redis, NATS. Frontend talks to mock API by default.
text:
Local development uses `docker compose` to run Postgres, Redis, and a
single in-memory NATS broker. The compose file lives at
`infra/local/docker-compose.yml`; `make up` and `make down` wrap it so
you do not need to remember the file path.

The frontend talks to a mock API by default; flip the `USE_REAL_API`
environment variable to point at the backend services running through
compose.

title: Developer environment
context_summary: Repo ships editor config + pyright strict; pre-commit rejects new type errors.
text:
The repository ships `.editorconfig`, `.vscode/settings.json`, and a
`pyrightconfig.json` so that VS Code and most JetBrains IDEs pick up
the right formatter and type checker without per-engineer tweaks.

Pyright runs in strict mode for every Python package. The
pre-commit hooks reject pushes that introduce new type errors, so run
`uv run pyright` locally before you push.

title: Expenses
context_summary: Section 'Overview' of the 'Expenses' handbook page.
text:
Tlaltipac reimburses the costs that make remote work effective. The
policy is short on purpose: trust the team, audit afterwards.

title: Expenses
context_summary: Home office, co-working, conferences, work software covered. Off-sites booked through the company travel agent.
text:
The company reimburses home office equipment up to a thousand dollars
per year, a co-working stipend of two hundred dollars per month, and
conference attendance up to two thousand dollars per year. Software
subscriptions used for work are covered with no cap.

Travel for team off-sites is booked through the company travel agent
and does not count against any individual limit.

title: Expenses
context_summary: 30-day filing window via the expense tool; manager-routed; reimbursed in the next payroll. 90-day hard deadline.
text:
Upload the receipt to the company expense tool within thirty days of
the purchase. The tool routes the receipt to the employee's manager
for approval; once approved, the reimbursement is paid in the next
payroll cycle.

Expenses filed more than ninety days after the purchase date are not
reimbursable; this is a hard accounting deadline rather than a policy
choice.

title: Expenses
context_summary: Receipt per line item. Card statement screenshot is the accepted fallback when a vendor refuses to issue a receipt.
text:
A receipt is required for every line item, even small ones. The
finance team prefers a clear photo over a forwarded email when there
is a choice — the photo carries the date, the merchant, and the total
all in one frame.

If a vendor refuses to issue a receipt, attach a screenshot of the
card statement instead and add a short note to the expense submission.

title: Onboarding
context_summary: Section 'Overview' of the 'Onboarding' handbook page.
text:
Your first two weeks at Tlaltipac. The goal is to ship a small change
to production by the end of week two — not to read every internal doc.

title: Onboarding
context_summary: First-day checklist for new engineers: laptop, SSO, Slack, buddy walkthrough.
text:
Your manager sends you a Linear issue titled "Onboarding: <your name>"
on the morning of your start date. Work through the checklist top to
bottom; it links to every other section of this handbook in the right
order.

The day-one checklist covers laptop pickup, single sign-on
enrolment, joining the engineering Slack channel, and pairing with
your onboarding buddy for a one-hour walkthrough of the codebase.

title: Onboarding
context_summary: Week one is paired programming across services; no solo commits expected.
text:
Week one is paired programming. You sit in a daily pairing slot with a
different engineer each day so that by Friday you have touched every
major service. There is no expectation that you push code on your own.

Read `handbook/dev-environment.md` before your first pairing slot so
that your laptop is ready. If anything in that doc is out of date,
file a pull request against this repository as your first contribution.

title: Onboarding
context_summary: Week two: ship a good-first-issue end-to-end, including code review and deployment.
text:
Week two you pick up a `good-first-issue` from Linear and ship it to
production end-to-end: write the change, open the pull request, get it
reviewed under the rules in `handbook/code-review.md`, and walk it
through the release process described in `handbook/deployment.md`.

By Friday of week two you should have one commit in production and one
incident response drill behind you. Your manager schedules a short
retrospective the following Monday.

title: Security
context_summary: Section 'Overview' of the 'Security' handbook page.
text:
Tlaltipac is SOC 2 Type I; the renewal audit lands in Q3. The rules
below are written to keep that audit clean and to keep the production
environment uneventful.

title: Security
context_summary: Every secret in the password manager. gitleaks pre-commit. Rotate first, file the report after.
text:
Every secret lives in the company password manager. There are no
secrets in the repository, in Slack messages, or in pull request
descriptions. The `gitleaks` pre-commit hook scans every staged change.

If a secret leaks anyway, treat it as an active incident: rotate the
credential first, then file the incident report. Do not wait for
guidance — rotation is always cheaper than the alternative.

title: Security
context_summary: Every internal tool sits behind SSO. New employees enrolled day one. Non-SSO tools need security-lead approval.
text:
Every internal tool sits behind the company identity provider. New
employees are enrolled on day one as part of the laptop pickup
process. Any tool that cannot be wired into single sign-on requires
written approval from the security lead before it is adopted.

title: Security
context_summary: Anyone can declare an incident. First responder posts to #incidents, opens runbook, pages on-call; PIR within five days.
text:
A production incident is anything that takes a customer-facing surface
down, exposes data, or violates a contractual service level. Anyone
on the team can declare an incident; declaring early is preferred to
declaring late.

The first responder posts the incident in the `#incidents` Slack
channel, opens a runbook from the wiki, and pages the on-call engineer
for the affected service. A post-incident review is written within
five business days and published to the engineering channel.

title: Time off
context_summary: Section 'Overview' of the 'Time off' handbook page.
text:
Tlaltipac runs an unlimited paid time off policy with a few opinionated
guardrails so that unlimited does not collapse into "nobody takes any".

title: Time off
context_summary: Unlimited PTO with a 20-day annual minimum tracked in HR and on manager dashboards.
text:
Every full-time employee takes at least twenty paid days off per year.
The minimum is tracked in the company HR tool and surfaced on the
manager's quarterly dashboard. Anyone trending below the minimum mid-year
gets a friendly reminder from their manager.

title: Time off
context_summary: Two-week notice for absences longer than a day; on-call rotation must be re-balanced first.
text:
File the request at least two weeks before the start date for any
absence longer than a single day. Same-day or next-day absences only
need a Slack note to your manager and your team channel.

The request automatically blocks the calendar of anyone who is part of
an overlapping on-call rotation; the on-call schedule needs to be
re-balanced before the request is approved.

title: Time off
context_summary: Public holidays follow each employee's country of residence; additional observances filed as normal PTO.
text:
Tlaltipac observes the national public holidays of each employee's
country of residence. The holiday list is maintained in the HR tool
and refreshed every December for the following year.

If you celebrate a holiday that is not on the list — for example a
religious observance — file a time-off request as usual; there is no
expectation that you justify it.

title: Welcome to Tlaltipac
context_summary: Section 'Overview' of the 'Welcome to Tlaltipac' handbook page.
text:
Tlaltipac is a fictional 40-person Series A SaaS company used as the
sample knowledge base for this Ajolopy example. Everything in this
handbook is invented and exists only so the agent has something
concrete to retrieve and cite.

title: Welcome to Tlaltipac
context_summary: Company background for the sample handbook: a fictional 40-person Series A SaaS used as the RAG fixture.
text:
Tlaltipac builds observability tooling for distributed agent runtimes.
The company was founded in 2025 and raised a 12 million dollar Series
A in early 2026. Most of the team works remotely; the legal seat is in
Mexico City and there is a small hub in Berlin.

title: Welcome to Tlaltipac
context_summary: Index of the sample handbook's eight files so retrieval lands on the right page.
text:
The handbook is the source of truth for how Tlaltipac operates. It is
split into short topical files so that contextual chunking has clean
boundaries to work with:

- `handbook/welcome.md` — this page.
- `handbook/onboarding.md` — first week for new engineers.
- `handbook/dev-environment.md` — local development setup.
- `handbook/code-review.md` — pull request etiquette.
- `handbook/security.md` — secrets handling and incident response.
- `handbook/deployment.md` — how releases reach production.
- `handbook/time-off.md` — paid time off and holidays.
- `handbook/expenses.md` — expense reimbursement.

title: Welcome to Tlaltipac
context_summary: Authoring convention: one H1 title plus short H2 sections so header-based chunking has clean boundaries.
text:
Every file is structured as a series of H2 sections so the retriever
can chunk along section boundaries. If you are adding a page, follow
the same convention: a single H1 title, then short H2 sections of one
to four paragraphs each.
